I would keep the year simple and familiar. In Quzhou County, the steadiest way for me to farm is the usual winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 71, so I would not choose crops that need a lot of hand labor or risky market timing. I would stay with grain crops I know, use improved or hybrid seed, and manage the land in a straightforward way: base fertilizer before sowing, a few irrigations when the crop really needs water, and only a limited number of pesticide sprays when pests or disease pressure show up. I would use machinery where possible and avoid anything too complicated, because for me stable yield and manageable labor matter more than chasing high risk, high effort returns.
